method: Instantiate each current VehicleVisual with its profile; inspect mesh surfaces, active material identities, skin bindings and imported LOD arrays through the engine.
scope: Full-resolution runtime model geometry after wheel separation and rider attachment, counting each surface once. These are not visible-triangle counts, render-pass totals, measured draw calls, GPU timings or FPS.
findings: The Porsche has the largest full-resolution geometry and surface budget: 325 chassis meshes plus 36 wheel meshes.
All four model imports already enable automatic LOD generation and shadow meshes; current visual instances use lod_bias=0.6.
Each counted mesh instance references a separate mesh resource in this audit; a same-resource MultiMesh conversion is not an immediate drop-in optimization.
The Yamaha including its rider has 99 skinned mesh instances. Baking or merging without preserving those bindings can damage deformation, wheel movement and the rider.
The Ferrari runtime axle splitter creates eight wheel meshes without copied imported LOD arrays; those wheel meshes total 21648 base triangles.
Blind merging can discard existing LODs, skin bindings, material selections and per-wheel transforms. A smaller mesh-instance count alone does not establish lower GPU time.
decision: Preserve existing source assets, LODs, wheels, skeletons and paint/livery behavior for this release. No new mesh baking or merging was introduced.
existing_mitigation: Adaptive render quality changes LOD threshold, 3D scale, shadow quality and tagged scenery distance. F8 records actual frame measurements and draw calls on the playing device.
future_optimization: Prioritize an independently generated Porsche render asset with chassis/material grouping and an explicit LOD chain; preserve the four independent wheel groups and paint targets. Validate appearance, transforms, bounds and measured GPU frame time before replacing the current model.
